description: The builder working a session: cooperative, concrete, states operating rules with conditions and scope when asked how things should be done.

turns.text: From the minutes I have, two people could sign, but in practice nothing went out without the advisor seeing it first.
turns.note: plain factual answer to an agenda question

turns.text: Never state a number without naming where it came from first. Cite the source, then the figure — that applies to every draft, internal or not.
turns.note: judgment-shaped rule: citation policy with scope

turns.text: The dual-approval rule only applied to payments over two hundred dollars; below that one signature was enough.
Never pad estimates in internal documents. For client-facing estimates, pad by fifteen percent and say that you did.
turns.note: judgment-shaped rule: estimation policy with an exception

turns.text: I decide what is visible to whom. Default everything to private and ask me before widening anything.
Honestly I don't remember the exact date that changed. The later minutes are probably the more reliable record.
If a draft is going to someone outside the team, I want to approve it before it is sent. Routine internal notes can go without me.
turns.note: judgment-shaped rule: outbound approval with a scope condition

turns.text: Yes, that matches what I remember — the storage unit came later, after the second fundraiser.
turns.note: confirmation with a small factual addition

turns.text: When two records disagree, show me both and let me pick. Do not average them and do not silently prefer the newer one.
That covers everything I know about it. Anything else you need, ask the advisor's handover notes.
